rv.q: Exquisitely precise, playfully elliptical and profoundly disturbing, this play by Caryl Churchill was astonishing when it premiered at London’s Royal Court Theatre in 2016, and remains so in Joanna Bowman’s superb revival – its Scottish premiere.
It’s a hugely impressive piece of theatre.
The energy of it is extraordinary.
Churchill admirers will find more than enough to savour, but it’s unlikely to make any converts amongst the hundred people who couldn’t name her on Pointless .
Escaped Alone is an enthralling theatrical experience that offers exceptional performances, poignant dialogue, and a profound exploration of the human condition.

cn.t: Churchill's dystopian modern classic receives a superb Scottish premiere, with critics praising its exquisitely precise writing and profoundly disturbing exploration of elderly women's lives that shifts from light-hearted tea chat to darker depths.
